## Analysis Workflow

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Raw 10x Data<br/>H5 files] --> B[Quality Control]
    B --> C{Pass QC?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Dimensionality Reduction<br/>PCA, UMAP, tSNE]
    C -->|No| B1[Filter cells/genes<br/>Adjust thresholds]
    B1 --> B
    
    D --> E{Batch Effects?}
    E -->|Yes| F[Data Integration<br/>BBKNN, Harmony, Combat, Scanorama]
    E -->|No| G[Clustering]
    F --> G
    
    G --> H{Good Clusters?}
    H -->|No| G1[Adjust resolution<br/>Check markers]
    G1 --> G
    H -->|Yes| I[Cell Type Annotation]
    
    I --> J{Annotate how?}
    J -->|Reference-based| K[Celltypist, Label Transfer, Ingest]
    J -->|Marker-based| L[Gene Set Enrichment]
    K --> M[Validated Cell Types]
    L --> M
    
    M --> N{Research Question?}
    N -->|Find cell type markers| O[Differential Expression<br/>Cluster biomarkers]
    N -->|Compare conditions| P[Differential Expression<br/>COVID vs Control]
    N -->|Understand development| Q[Trajectory Inference<br/>PAGA, CellRank]
    
    O --> R[Biological Interpretation]
    P --> S[Pathway Enrichment<br/>GSEA]
    Q --> T[Lineage Analysis<br/>Driver genes]
    
    S --> R
    T --> R
    
    R --> U[Publication/<br/>Further Experiments]
    
    style B fill:#e1f5ff
    style F fill:#fff4e1
    style G fill:#ffe1f5
    style I fill:#e1ffe1

    style Q fill:#ffe1e1

```

## Step-by-Step Guide

### 1. Quality Control {.step}

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Purpose

**Biological Questions:**

- Which cells are high quality vs. damaged/dying?
- Are there technical artifacts (doublets, empty droplets)?
- Is there batch variation between samples?
- Are samples well-prepared or contaminated?

**Key Decisions:**

- Mitochondrial % cutoff (typically <20%)
- Minimum genes per cell (typically >200)
- Ribosomal % minimum (typically >5%)
- Sex balance across conditions
- Cell cycle state distribution

#### Inputs

- Raw count matrices (`.h5` files from 10x)
- Sample metadata (COVID vs. Control, patient IDs)

#### Outputs

- **Filtered AnnData object** (`scanpy_covid_qc.h5ad`)
- **QC metrics** in `adata.obs`:
  - `n_genes_by_counts`, `total_counts`
  - `pct_counts_mt`, `pct_counts_ribo`, `pct_counts_hb`
  - `doublet_scores`, `predicted_doublets`
  - `percent_chrY`, `XIST-counts`
  - `S_score`, `G2M_score`, `phase`

#### Red Flags

- 🚩 >50% cells filtered from any sample
- 🚩 Bimodal MT% distribution
- 🚩 Sex imbalance between conditions
- 🚩 Doublet rate >10%
- 🚩 Sample-specific quality issues

:::

---

### 2. Dimensionality Reduction {.step}

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Purpose

**Biological Questions:**

- What are the major sources of variation in the data?
- How many principal components capture biological signal?
- Can we visualize cell-to-cell relationships?
- Are there distinct cell populations?
- Do technical factors drive separation?

**Key Decisions:**

- Number of highly variable genes (typically 2000-3000)
- Number of PCs to use (typically 30-50)
- UMAP/tSNE parameters (neighbors, spread, perplexity)
- Which covariates to regress out

#### Inputs

- QC-filtered data (`scanpy_covid_qc.h5ad`)
- Normalized, log-transformed counts

#### Outputs

- **AnnData with embeddings** (`scanpy_covid_qc_dr.h5ad`)
- **`adata.var.highly_variable`**: Boolean for HVGs
- **`adata.obsm['X_pca']`**: PCA coordinates
- **`adata.obsm['X_umap']`**: UMAP coordinates  
- **`adata.obsm['X_tsne']`**: tSNE coordinates
- **`adata.uns['pca']['variance_ratio']`**: Variance explained

#### Red Flags

- 🚩 First PC explains >30% variance (technical effect)
- 🚩 No clear structure in UMAP/tSNE
- 🚩 Samples separate completely (batch effect)
- 🚩 QC metrics drive embeddings
- 🚩 PCA loadings dominated by MT/ribo genes

:::

---

### 3. Data Integration {.step}

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Purpose

**Biological Questions:**

- Are observed differences biological or technical?
- Do samples/batches confound biological signals?
- Can we fairly compare COVID vs. Control?
- Which cell types are present across all samples?

**Key Decisions:**

- Which integration method (BBKNN, Harmony, Combat, Scanorama)?
- How aggressive should correction be?
- Batch-aware vs. global HVG selection?
- Validate integration success?

#### Inputs

- Dimensionality-reduced data (`scanpy_covid_qc_dr.h5ad`)
- Batch/sample metadata

#### Outputs

- **Multiple integrated embeddings** (`scanpy_covid_qc_dr_int.h5ad`)
- **`adata.obsm['X_pca_harmony']`**: Harmony-corrected PCA
- **`adata.obsm['X_umap_bbknn']`**: BBKNN UMAP
- **`adata.obsm['X_umap_combat']`**: Combat UMAP
- **`adata.obsm['X_umap_scanorama']`**: Scanorama UMAP

#### Method Selection

| **Method** | **Best For** | **Modifies** |
|------------|--------------|--------------|
| **BBKNN** | Clustering, tight clusters | Neighbor graph |
| **Harmony** | Trajectories, continuous processes | PCA space |
| **Combat** | Differential expression | Gene expression |
| **Scanorama** | Heterogeneous batches | Low-dim embedding |

#### Red Flags

- 🚩 Perfect mixing with no structure (over-correction)
- 🚩 No mixing improvement (under-correction)
- 🚩 Methods completely disagree
- 🚩 COVID vs. Control signal lost

:::

---

### 4. Clustering {.step}

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Purpose

**Biological Questions:**

- How many distinct cell populations exist?
- What are the major cell types?
- Are there subtypes within cell types?
- How are cell populations related?
- Are clusters biologically meaningful or technical?

**Key Decisions:**

- Clustering resolution (0.4-1.4)
- Use integrated or unintegrated data?
- Merge over-split clusters?
- Subcluster specific populations?

#### Inputs

- Integrated data (`scanpy_covid_qc_dr_int.h5ad`)
- Neighbor graph

#### Outputs

- **Clustered data** (`scanpy_covid_qc_dr_int_cl.h5ad`)
- **`adata.obs['leiden_0.4']`**: Coarse clusters
- **`adata.obs['leiden_0.6']`**: Medium resolution
- **`adata.obs['leiden_1.0']`**: Fine resolution
- **`adata.obs['leiden_1.4']`**: Very fine resolution
- **Cluster dendrograms**: Relationships

#### Resolution Guide

| **Resolution** | **Use Case** | **Typical # Clusters** |
|----------------|--------------|------------------------|
| 0.4 | Major lineages | 5-10 |
| 0.6 | Cell types | 8-15 |
| 1.0 | Subtypes | 12-20 |
| 1.4 | Cell states | 15-30 |

#### Red Flags

- 🚩 Clusters defined by QC metrics, not biology
- 🚩 Housekeeping genes as top markers
- 🚩 Sample-specific clusters
- 🚩 No clear marker genes
- 🚩 Unrelated cell types in same cluster

:::

---

### 5. Differential Gene Expression {.step}

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Purpose

**Biological Questions:**

**Cluster biomarkers:**
- What genes define each cell type?
- Can we identify clusters biologically?
- Which genes are specific vs. shared?

**Condition comparisons:**
- How does COVID-19 affect specific cell types?
- Which pathways are activated/suppressed?
- Are changes cell-type-specific or global?

**Key Decisions:**

- Statistical test (Wilcoxon recommended)
- Fold-change and p-value cutoffs
- Compare per cluster or globally?
- How to handle patient variability?

#### Inputs

- Clustered data (`scanpy_covid_qc_dr_int_cl.h5ad`)
- Normalized, log-transformed counts in `adata.raw`

#### Outputs

- **DGE results** (`scanpy_covid_qc_dr_scanorama_cl_dge.h5ad`)
- **`adata.uns['rank_genes_groups']`**: All DE results
  - `names`: Gene names
  - `scores`: Test statistics
  - `pvals_adj`: Adjusted p-values
  - `logfoldchanges`: Effect sizes
- **Pathway enrichment results**: GO/KEGG terms

#### Two Modes

**1. Cluster biomarkers:**
```python
sc.tl.rank_genes_groups(adata, 'leiden_0.6', method='wilcoxon')
# Compares each cluster vs. all others
```

**2. Condition comparison:**
```python
# Subset to one cluster first
monocytes = adata[adata.obs['cell_type']=='Monocytes']
sc.tl.rank_genes_groups(monocytes, 'type', method='wilcoxon')
# Compares COVID vs. Control within monocytes
```

#### Red Flags

- 🚩 Sex chromosome genes as top DE (sex imbalance)
- 🚩 Patient-specific genes (dominated by one individual)
- 🚩 Housekeeping genes enriched (technical issues)
- 🚩 No pathway enrichment (noisy gene list)
- 🚩 Unbalanced cell numbers per sample

:::

---

### 6. Cell Type Annotation {.step}

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Purpose

**Biological Questions:**

- What cell types are present?
- How confident are our annotations?
- Are there novel/unexpected populations?
- Do annotations agree across methods?

**Key Decisions:**

- Reference-based vs. marker-based?
- Which reference dataset to use?
- Which Celltypist model (Low vs. High resolution)?
- Trust automatic predictions or manual curation?

#### Inputs

- Clustered data (`scanpy_covid_qc_dr_int_cl.h5ad`)
- Reference dataset (pbmc3k or custom)
- Marker gene lists

#### Outputs

- **Annotated data** (`scanpy_covid_qc_dr_int_cl_ct-ctrl13.h5ad`)
- **Multiple prediction columns**:
  - `louvain` (Ingest)
  - `label_trans` (Scanorama label transfer)
  - `predicted_labels` (Celltypist per-cell)
  - `majority_voting` (Celltypist smoothed)
  - `GS_overlap_pred` (Marker gene enrichment)

#### Method Comparison

| **Method** | **Strength** | **Limitation** |
|------------|--------------|----------------|
| **Label Transfer** | Uses integration, smooth | Needs good reference alignment |
| **Ingest** | Fast, scalable | Query doesn't influence reference |
| **Celltypist Pretrained** | Large training data, detailed | May predict irrelevant subtypes |
| **Celltypist Custom** | Matched to your data | Limited by reference size |
| **Marker Gene Sets** | Transparent, interpretable | Limited resolution |

#### Red Flags

- 🚩 Methods completely disagree
- 🚩 Predictions scattered randomly
- 🚩 Unexpected cell types (check doublets)
- 🚩 Poor spatial coherence
- 🚩 Predictions don't match markers

:::

---

### 7. Trajectory Inference {.step}

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Purpose

**Biological Questions:**

- How do cells differentiate/develop?
- What are the lineage relationships?
- Which genes drive fate decisions?
- When do cells commit to specific fates?
- What are the branch points?

**Key Decisions:**

- Which cells are initial/terminal states?
- How many neighbors for trajectory graph?
- Use pseudotime, RNA velocity, or both?
- Which lineages to analyze in detail?

#### Inputs

- Annotated data with cell types
- Batch-corrected embeddings
- (Optional) RNA velocity data

#### Outputs

- **PAGA graph**: Global trajectory topology
- **Pseudotime** (`dpt_pseudotime`): Developmental ordering
- **Fate probabilities**: Probability for each terminal state
- **Driver genes**: Genes correlated with each fate
- **Gene trends**: Expression dynamics along trajectories

#### When to Use

**Appropriate for:**

- ✅ Developmental systems (hematopoiesis, organogenesis)
- ✅ Differentiation processes (iPSC → neurons)
- ✅ Cell activation (resting → activated immune cells)
- ✅ Disease progression (healthy → disease states)

**Not appropriate for:**

- ❌ Purely discrete cell types (no transitions)
- ❌ Cross-sectional data without time component
- ❌ When all cells are terminally differentiated

#### Red Flags

- 🚩 Cycles in trajectory (should be directional)
- 🚩 Impossible connections (unrelated lineages)
- 🚩 Driver genes not lineage-specific
- 🚩 Pseudotime doesn't match biology
- 🚩 Terminal states are progenitors

:::

---

    Start -->|Compare conditions| B[QC → DimRed → Integrate → Cluster → Annotate → DGE]

## Key Concepts Summary

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Clustering Groups Cells

**NOT genes!**

- Each **cell** is a data point with expression for ~20,000 genes
- Clustering groups **cells** with similar expression profiles
- Result: Cell type/state identification

**Common confusion:** "Why isn't there a housekeeping gene cluster?"

- Answer: ALL cells express housekeeping genes similarly
- Clustering finds what makes cells **different**, not same
- Housekeeping genes are typically excluded from clustering

### Markers vs Drivers

**Marker genes** (from DGE):

- Identify what a cell type **is**
- Define cell identity
- Used for annotation
- Example: CD3E marks T cells

**Driver genes** (from trajectory):

- Identify what **makes** cells become a type
- Control differentiation/activation
- Causal relationships (potentially)
- Example: GATA1 drives erythrocyte fate

Both are differentially expressed, but conceptually different!

### Integration ≠ Batch Correction

**Batch correction** (broader term):

- Any method to remove technical variation
- Can be done at various stages
- Includes regression, normalization, etc.

**Integration** (specific):

- Aligning multiple datasets/samples
- Creates shared embedding space
- Specific algorithms (Harmony, Scanorama, etc.)
- Subset of batch correction methods

All integration is batch correction, but not all batch correction is integration.

### Pseudotime ≠ Real Time

**Pseudotime**:

- Computational ordering of cells
- Represents developmental **progress**
- NOT hours/days of development
- Relative, not absolute
- Cannot compare across lineages directly

**Real time**: Calendar time (which we don't have in snapshot data)

Pseudotime is inferred from expression similarity, assuming similar cells are at similar stages.

:::

## Common Pitfalls

::: {.callout-warning}
## Critical Mistakes to Avoid

### Data Management

1. **❌ Forgetting to save raw counts**
   - `adata.raw = adata` BEFORE normalization
   - Can't recover raw counts after scaling

2. **❌ Using wrong matrix for DGE**
   - Use `adata.raw` (normalized, log-transformed, ALL genes)
   - NOT `adata.X` (scaled, HVGs only)

3. **❌ Comparing pseudotime across lineages**
   - Pseudotime only meaningful within a lineage
   - 0.5 in erythrocytes ≠ 0.5 in T cells

### Statistical Issues

4. **❌ Ignoring confounders**
   - Sex, age, batch, sample quality
   - Will create false DE genes

5. **❌ Unbalanced sample sizes in DGE**
   - One sample with 200 cells dominates over sample with 30 cells
   - Subsample or use pseudobulk

6. **❌ Multiple testing without correction**
   - Testing 20,000 genes → many false positives
   - Use FDR/Bonferroni correction

### Biological Interpretation

7. **❌ Over-interpreting cluster numbers**
   - Clusters are computational, not absolute truth
   - Cell types exist on continua

8. **❌ Trusting single method**
   - Integration: try multiple, check consensus
   - Annotation: validate with markers
   - Never rely on one algorithm alone

9. **❌ Ignoring biological knowledge**
   - Algorithms don't know biology
   - Impossible cell types mean errors
   - Literature validation essential

:::

## Analysis Checklist

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

### Before Starting

- [ ] Understand biological system
- [ ] Know expected cell types

**QC:**

- [ ] Reasonable cell numbers retained (>50%)
- [ ] QC metrics look normal
- [ ] Samples comparable quality

**Dimensionality Reduction:**

- [ ] Elbow plot shows clear signal
- [ ] PC loadings are interpretable
- [ ] UMAP shows structure
- [ ] Batch effects identified
- [ ] Saved: `scanpy_covid_qc_dr.h5ad`

**Integration:**

- [ ] Samples mix within cell types
- [ ] Cell types remain separated
- [ ] Multiple methods agree
- [ ] COVID signal preserved
- [ ] Saved: `scanpy_covid_qc_dr_int.h5ad`

**Clustering:**

- [ ] Spatially coherent clusters
- [ ] Clear marker genes
- [ ] Biologically interpretable
- [ ] Not driven by technical factors
- [ ] Saved: `scanpy_covid_qc_dr_int_cl.h5ad`

**Annotation:**

- [ ] Consensus across methods
- [ ] Markers support predictions
- [ ] All major types identified
- [ ] Documented uncertainties
- [ ] Saved: `scanpy_covid_qc_dr_int_cl_ct.h5ad`

**DGE/Trajectory:**

- [ ] Results make biological sense
- [ ] Validated with literature
- [ ] Confounders addressed
- [ ] Ready for publication/validation

:::

## Biological Questions → Analysis Path

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Cell Type Discovery

**Question:** *What cell types are in my sample?*

**Path:**

1. ✅ **QC**: Remove low-quality cells
2. ✅ **DimRed**: Visualize major populations
3. ✅ **Clustering**: Separate populations
4. ✅ **DGE (markers)**: Find defining genes
5. ✅ **Annotation**: Assign biological identities

**Skip:** Integration (unless multiple batches), Trajectory

**Output:** Annotated cell type map

---

### Disease Response

**Question:** *How does COVID-19 affect immune cells?*

**Path:**

1. ✅ **QC**: Ensure quality comparable between groups
2. ✅ **DimRed**: Identify populations
3. ✅ **Integration**: Remove batch effects (critical!)
4. ✅ **Clustering**: Identify cell types
5. ✅ **Annotation**: Label cell types
6. ✅ **DGE (condition)**: Compare COVID vs. Control **per cell type**
7. ✅ **Pathway enrichment**: Interpret gene lists

**Don't skip:** Integration (samples may have batch effects)

**Output:** Cell-type-specific disease signatures

---

### Biomarker Discovery

**Question:** *What genes mark each cell type?*

**Path:**

1. ✅ **QC**: High-quality cells only
2. ✅ **DimRed**: Separate populations
3. ✅ **Clustering**: Define populations
4. ✅ **DGE (cluster markers)**: Find top genes per cluster
5. ✅ **Validation**: Check specificity on UMAP/dotplots

**May skip:** Integration (if single batch), Annotation (exploratory)

**Output:** Marker gene lists for cell types

---

### Developmental Biology

**Question:** *How do stem cells differentiate into specific types?*

**Path:**

1. ✅ **QC**: Remove doublets (critical for trajectories)
2. ✅ **DimRed**: Visualize differentiation continuum
3. ✅ **Integration**: If multiple samples
4. ✅ **Clustering**: Identify developmental stages
5. ✅ **Annotation**: Label progenitors and mature types
6. ✅ **Trajectory**: PAGA + pseudotime + CellRank
7. ✅ **Driver genes**: Find fate determinants

**Critical:** Must have continuous data (progenitors + intermediates + mature)

**Output:** Developmental trajectories and driver genes

:::

## Quick Reference

### Most Important Commands

```python
# QC
sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics(adata, qc_vars=['mt','ribo'])
sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_genes=200)
sc.pp.filter_genes(adata, min_cells=3)

# Normalization & Scaling
adata.raw = adata  # SAVE FIRST!
sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4)
sc.pp.log1p(adata)
sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, n_top_genes=2000)
sc.pp.regress_out(adata, ['total_counts', 'pct_counts_mt'])
sc.pp.scale(adata, max_value=10)

# Dimensionality Reduction
sc.pp.pca(adata)
sc.pp.neighbors(adata, n_neighbors=20, n_pcs=30)
sc.tl.umap(adata)

# Integration
import harmonypy as hm
sc.external.pp.bbknn(adata, 'sample')
# Or Harmony, Combat, Scanorama

# Clustering
sc.tl.leiden(adata, resolution=0.6)

# DGE
sc.tl.rank_genes_groups(adata, 'leiden', method='wilcoxon')

# Annotation
import celltypist
predictions = celltypist.annotate(adata, model='Immune_All_High.pkl')

# Trajectory
sc.tl.paga(adata, groups='celltype')
sc.tl.dpt(adata)  # pseudotime
```

### Common Parameter Values

| **Parameter** | **Typical Range** | **Default** | **Notes** |
|---------------|-------------------|-------------|-----------|
| `min_genes` | 200-500 | 200 | Minimum genes per cell |
| `min_cells` | 3-10 | 3 | Minimum cells per gene |
| `pct_counts_mt` | <10-20% | <20% | MT% cutoff |
| `n_top_genes` (HVG) | 1000-4000 | 2000 | Highly variable genes |
| `n_pcs` | 20-50 | 30-50 | PCs for neighbors |
| `n_neighbors` | 10-30 | 15-20 | KNN graph |
| `resolution` | 0.4-1.4 | 1.0 | Leiden clustering |
| `min_dist` (UMAP) | 0.1-0.5 | 0.3 | UMAP spread |

### Visualization Cheat Sheet

```python
# Cell-level visualization
sc.pl.umap(adata, color='gene_name')  # Gene expression
sc.pl.umap(adata, color='cluster')    # Clusters
sc.pl.umap(adata, color='sample')     # Batch effects

# Cluster-level visualization
sc.pl.dotplot(adata, genes, groupby='cluster')        # Expression + detection
sc.pl.heatmap(adata, genes, groupby='cluster')        # Expression heatmap
sc.pl.violin(adata, genes, groupby='cluster')         # Distributions
sc.pl.matrixplot(adata, genes, groupby='cluster')     # Clean matrix

# QC visualization
sc.pl.violin(adata, ['n_genes', 'pct_counts_mt'], groupby='sample')
sc.pl.scatter(adata, x='total_counts', y='pct_counts_mt', color='sample')

# Trajectory visualization
sc.pl.paga(adata, color='celltype')                   # Abstract graph
sc.pl.draw_graph(adata, color='pseudotime')           # Cell-level trajectory
```
